Simulate genetic covariance matrices from a known conductance surface

Source: R/genetic_distance.R
simulate_covariance_response.Rd

Simulates one or more covariance response matrices from a known conductance-resistance relationship, using the same Wishart covariance model fitted by wishart_covariance.

Usage

simulate_covariance_response(
  theta,
  formula,
  data,
  conductance_model = loglinear_conductance,
  tau = 1,
  sigma = 0,
  nu,
  nsim = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  cores = 1L
)

Arguments

theta

Conductance parameters. May be supplied as a numeric vector or a one-row matrix. If unnamed, values are matched in the order implied by formula. Gaussian sigma.<layer> parameters use the map units reported by coef(); conversion to optimizer units is internal.

formula

Model formula specifying the conductance covariates. The left hand side, if supplied, is ignored.

data

A conductance_surface object.

conductance_model

Conductance-model factory, such as loglinear_conductance.

tau

Nonnegative scaling applied to the conductance-implied covariance matrix, on the same scale as the fitted Wishart tau.

sigma

Nonnegative nugget variance added to the diagonal, on its natural (variance) scale. This differs from the fitted sigma reported for wishart_covariance and generalized_wishart, which is the logarithm of the nugget variance. To simulate from a fitted model, pass exp() of the fitted sigma.

nu

Effective Wishart degrees of freedom: controls the amount of sampling noise in the simulated covariance: larger nu gives tighter draws around Sigma. This is a model assumption, not a marker count or an estimate of information from biological data. Examine a range of plausible values. The simulation requires nu to be at least the covariance-matrix dimension. See wishart_covariance for how nu propagates into estimation (it scales standard errors and model-selection statistics but not point estimates).

nsim

Number of covariance matrices to simulate.

seed

Optional random seed.

cores

Number of cores passed to terradish_distance.

Value

A list containing:

covariance

A covariance matrix if nsim = 1, otherwise a three-dimensional array of simulated covariance matrices.

Sigma

The covariance matrix used as the Wishart scale matrix after applying tau and sigma.

E

The conductance-implied covariance matrix returned by terradish_distance(covariance = TRUE).

theta

The validated conductance parameter matrix used for simulation.

tau

The supplied tau.

sigma

The supplied sigma (nugget variance, natural scale).

nu

The supplied nu.

Details

The helper first computes the conductance-implied covariance matrix E(theta) from the supplied resistance surface. It then forms Sigma = tau * E(theta) + sigma * I and simulates S ~ Wishart(nu, Sigma) / nu. This makes the returned covariance matrices directly compatible with wishart_covariance. These results are internal to the assumed model. Simulating and fitting at the same incorrect nu cannot reveal that error. Use covariance_response_power with different nu and nu_fit to examine its effect on coverage.

See also

covariance_response_power, wishart_covariance

Other simulation and study design: covariance_response_power(), print.terradish_covariance_power()

Examples

r1 <- terra::rast(nrows = 3, ncols = 3, xmin = 0, xmax = 3, ymin = 0,
                  ymax = 3, vals = 1:9)
r2 <- terra::rast(nrows = 3, ncols = 3, xmin = 0, xmax = 3, ymin = 0,
                  ymax = 3, vals = c(9, 1, 4, 3, 8, 2, 5, 7, 6))
covariates <- c(r1, r2)
names(covariates) <- c("x1", "x2")
pts <- terra::vect(matrix(c(0.5, 0.5,
                           1.5, 1.5,
                           2.5, 2.5), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE),
                   type = "points")
surface <- conductance_surface(covariates, pts, directions = 4)
sim <- simulate_covariance_response(
  theta = c(x1 = 0.3, x2 = -0.2),
  formula = ~ x1 + x2,
  data = surface,
  tau = 0.8,
  sigma = 0.5,
  nu = 20,
  seed = 1
)
sim$covariance
#>            [,1]       [,2]       [,3]
#> [1,]  0.4538078  0.1349725 -0.2132605
#> [2,]  0.1349725  0.7820864 -0.2164368
#> [3,] -0.2132605 -0.2164368  0.7259222
